cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Uncle – the brother of one's father or mother, or the husband of one's aunt.

p.em: Example: My uncle John took me to my very first baseball game when I was ten.

cosy-blockquote.p: Aunt – the sister of one's father or mother, or the wife of one's uncle.

p.em: Example: My aunt Mary always bakes delicious chocolate chip cookies for my birthday.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nephew – a son of one's brother or sister.

p.em: Example: He has one nephew who is studying computer science at university.

cosy-blockquote.p: Niece – a daughter of one's brother or sister.

p.em: Example: My niece is five years old and she loves drawing pictures of cats.

cosy-blockquote.p: Relative – a person connected by blood or marriage.

p.em: Example: Almost all my relatives gather together at my grandparents' house for Christmas.

cosy-blockquote.p: Generation – all of the people born and living at about the same time.

p.em: Example: My grandparents' generation lived in a very different, quieter world.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gratitude ≠ ungratefulness – the quality of being thankful ≠ a lack of appreciation or thankfulness.

p.em: Example: Writing a thank-you note is a simple way to show gratitude instead of ungratefulness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gathering ≠ isolation – an assembly or meeting of people ≠ the state of being completely alone.

p.em: Example: Our cozy family gathering saved her from a painful sense of winter isolation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Traditional – existing in or as part of a long-established tradition or custom.

p.em: Example: It is traditional to exchange gifts and share a big dinner on New Year's Eve.

cosy-blockquote.p: Childhood – the state or period of being a child.

p.em: Example: She spent her childhood playing outdoors in a beautiful, sunny countryside.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What is the traditional role of an uncle in a classical family structure?
★ Do you have a favorite uncle who helped you during your youth?

How does an aunt's support differ from a mother's guidance?
★ What is the most memorable advice your aunt ever gave you?

Why is the relationship between an uncle and his nephew often so friendly and relaxed?
★ Do you have a nephew who is currently studying or working?

How can aunts play an active role in mentoring their niece's career or life choices?
★ How often do you buy birthday gifts for your niece?

Why do some people feel more comfortable sharing secrets with a distant relative than a parent?
★ Who is the most funny or unusual relative in your family?

How do cultural expectations change from one generation to the next regarding family duties?
★ Do you think your generation is more connected or less connected to family than your parents were?

Why is expressing gratitude to elderly relatives so important for community health?
★ How do you show gratitude when a relative gives you an unexpected gift?

Why are traditional family gatherings becoming less frequent in modern, busy cities?
★ What is your favorite food or activity during a family gathering?

What is the most beautiful traditional custom your family still practices today?
★ Do you prefer traditional holidays or do you prefer traveling alone?

How does a happy childhood with supportive relatives protect our mental health as adults?
★ What is the happiest memory from your childhood involving your relatives?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: the thank-you message task: Imagine you are writing a sweet postcard to your favorite aunt or uncle to celebrate this special day. What memories would you thank them for? Work as a team to compose a short, cozy message in English.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, digital communication will replace physical family gatherings entirely, leaving us isolated.
★ Do you prefer video calls or physical visits when speaking to your relatives?

The role of an uncle or aunt is less important today than it was in traditional societies.
★ Do you think modern children are too busy with screens to bond with their uncles?

Children who spend their childhood near many relatives grow up to be more confident and resilient.
★ Did you grow up in a big house with many relatives, or in a quiet apartment?

Showing gratitude is a skill that is slowly disappearing in the younger generation.
★ Do you think younger people are ungrateful, or are they just different?

A niece or nephew should always help their elderly relatives with technology and physical work.
★ Have you ever had to help an older relative use a smartphone or computer?

Maintaining traditional family hierarchies is essential to protect young children from moral confusion.
★ Do you think classical family traditions should be strictly followed or modernized?

Living in deep social isolation is better for creative work than living surrounded by a noisy family.
★ Where do you study best: in a quiet room alone, or in a busy café?

A distant relative has absolutely no right to give advice regarding a child's education or career choices.
★ Has a distant relative ever criticized your life decisions? How did you respond?

We should actively celebrate days like Aunt and Uncle Day to strengthen our community bonds.
★ Do you think celebrating minor holidays is fun or is it just a waste of time?

The next generation will have a completely different concept of family, built on shared interests rather than blood.
★ Do you consider your close friends as part of your family circle?

ul.li: Incorrect: My uncle John wife is Mary. → Correct: My uncle john's wife is Mary. ((Underlined error: possessive 's is required to show ownership or relationship))

Incorrect: I am very gratitude for my aunt's help. → Correct: I am very grateful for my aunt's help. ((Underlined word form error: 'gratitude' is a noun; the adjective form to describe how you feel is 'grateful'))
Incorrect: We had a very good family gather. → Correct: We had a very good family gathering. ((Underlined word form error: use the noun 'gathering' instead of the verb form 'gather'))
